metadata.title: Impact of PIRLS and TIMSS in low- and middle-income countries

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a questionnaire/instrument package commissioned by IEA (with World Bank officers) to collect stakeholders’ perceptions of the impact of PIRLS 2001 (and mentions TIMSS 2003). It does not provide an empirical student-level analysis of PIRLS/TIMSS microdata, nor does it describe sampling, scaling, or plausible-values (PV) estimation procedures. Because no student achievement outcomes are modeled here, there is no basis to specify which ILSA sampling weights (e.g., student design weights) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/JRR) would be applied. For any future empirical analysis using PIRLS/TIMSS microdata, analysts should use the official IEA sampling weights and PV procedures supplied with the international database, but those details are not contained in this questionnaire text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this document does not analyze PIRLS/TIMSS achievement scores at the student level; it is an impact questionnaire collecting qualitative/administrative responses (e.g., whether national reports were read, perceived curriculum relevance, and perceived policy changes). Since there is no PV-based dependent variable or PV estimation workflow described, PV handling is outside the scope of this instrument. Missing-data handling is not reported because the text does not present an empirical dataset, analytic sample construction, or statistical modeling results.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is defined in the provided text. Instead, the document contains questionnaires for (i) National Report Coordinators (NRC), (ii) Senior Education Officials (SEO), and (iii) World Bank Officers (WBO) in a set of countries that received World Bank funding support to participate in PIRLS 2001 and/or TIMSS 2003. The only explicit inclusion logic is that countries are those from which completed questionnaires/interviews were received (listed in Appendix 7). Therefore, there are no grade-level, item-level, or missing-response exclusion rules for student achievement data in this text.

data.outcome_summary: This document does not report empirical results from PIRLS/TIMSS microdata; it provides an impact-evaluation questionnaire intended to gather stakeholders’ perceptions of how PIRLS 2001 (and, by extension, TIMSS 2003) influenced education policy and practice in low- and middle-income countries supported by the World Bank. It describes the scope of the IEA studies (PIRLS 2001 and TIMSS 2003), the role of national reports and dissemination to senior officials and ministers, and the types of policy-relevant aspects stakeholders might highlight (e.g., international rankings, trends, content-area differences, and teaching methods). The instrument also asks about coverage in media, public discussion and curriculum change, and perceived importance of participation and future participation. Because no student achievement outcomes are modeled and no statistical analysis is presented, there are no performance metrics, benchmarks, or causal claims to interpret from this text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided article text is an instrument/questionnaire and supporting appendices rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, there is no reported student-level dataset, no analytic sample size, no PV handling strategy, no missing-data strategy for an estimation model, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics. The country list appears only as the set of countries from which questionnaires/interviews were received, not as a basis for statistical modeling in this excerpt.
